statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits in the low band on a compressed, two-way overnight tape with no observed one-way structure, while stress stays high on the unresolved Gulf war, halted Strait of Hormuz shipping and firmer crude.
recommendation: Overnight conditions remain consistent with a mean-reverting regime: NQ futures are grinding modestly higher inside a band only about 0.27% wide, with no failed retracements and no repeated extension observed. The mapped policy state is EA_ON, with a narrow danger window flagged around the US cash open and its first hour, where opening-auction structure is resolved.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a 0.3% overnight gain in a very tight, holiday-thinned Asian session as stalled US-Iran talks and halted Hormuz shipping keep crude firm
body: NQ futures trade near 30,245, about 0.34% above the prior 30,141.75 settlement, inside an overnight band of roughly 30,167.75-30,247.25 - a range of only about 0.27%. Price sits near the top of that band, but the band itself is narrow, retracements are present and no persistent directional efficiency or failed-retracement structure has been observed. S&P 500 futures are firmer by 0.10% inside a 0.13% range, confirming a compressed rather than trending overnight tape. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Friday at 30,046.14, down 0.13% inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range, close to its 30,762.20 52-week high, with the VIX at 14.25 near 2026 lows. Asian trade is subdued and thin: MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan is flat, the Nikkei is up 0.4%, Australia is down 0.3% and South Korea is closed for a public holiday. Japanese Q2 GDP grew an annualised 1.1%, below the 2.0% median forecast, on the first quarterly drop in private consumption in two years. The Gulf war remains unresolved and is the dominant stress channel. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Iran had not decided to resume talks with the United States, and Strait of Hormuz traffic has collapsed - five commodity vessels transited on Saturday and none registered on Sunday, against 31 the prior weekend. Crude has firmed accordingly, with Brent near $89.20 and WTI near $82.83 after weekly gains above 5%. Rates point the other way: the 2-year yield eased about 2bp to 4.156% and the 10-year about 1bp to 4.684% after soft US data, with fed funds futures implying roughly 70% odds of no change at the September 16 meeting, up from about 48% a month ago. Friday's tape showed a dispersed rather than one-directional AI complex: Broadcom fell 5.94% while AMD rose 6.5% and Micron 2.3%, leaving megacap breadth negative (six of eight lower) but with wide dispersion and semiconductors mixed on average. Delayed cross-asset context shows Nasdaq futures marginally firmer than the broader complex, VIX futures slightly bid, gold higher and Treasury futures modestly up, which is a conflicted rather than aligned configuration. That combination - compressed index ranges, unaligned cross-assets, no Tier-1 US release scheduled today and no observed no-retracement path - keeps tail risk in the low band despite genuinely high stress. The main structural checkpoint is the 13:30Z cash open, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the specific pattern capable of denying mean reversion; that structure is not observed in advance. FOMC minutes on 19 August at 18:00Z are the week's principal scheduled catalyst.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail stayed in the low band throughout, ranging from 12 to 17, with the mapped policy state EA_ON for the entire window. Stress peaked at 82 during Saturday's US-hours window as Gulf war and crude headlines dominated, then eased into the high band around 67-70 overnight as the tape compressed. Dominant mode was mixed through the weekend session and settled to normal from 23:00Z as two-way overnight rotation established itself.
outlookSummary: The conditional path keeps tail in the low band across all 24 forecast hours, with the mapped policy state EA_ON throughout. Conditional risk is lowest through the thin Asian and early European hours, rises modestly from the European cash open as real volume tests the narrow overnight band, and peaks at 18 across the 13:00Z-15:00Z window covering the US cash open, the opening auction and the NAHB release - the point at which opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would first become observable. It decays through the US afternoon, lifts again for the 19:00Z power hour where late-session continuation or reversal can be sharp, then returns to the overnight baseline after the 20:00Z cash close. Stress stays in the high band throughout on the unresolved Gulf war and halted Hormuz shipping. Confidence decays with forecast distance because current price-path evidence cannot be extended reliably across a full day.
